title: Rosetta App Workflow
description: Generic execution harness for an app: how to open it, how to dispatch an intent, how to verify, how to recover. One file per app at registry/apps/{app_id}/workflow.json. NOTE: the action sub-schemas in $defs (keyAction, keyComboAction, typeTextAction, clickAction, menuAction, openAppAction) are duplicated verbatim between workflow.schema.json and shortcut.schema.json. Any change to action types must touch both files. The validate-registry script lints that these $defs are byte-identical.

app_id.description: Must match the parent folder under registry/apps/ and the id in meta.json.

open.description: Action sequence that brings the app to a usable state when not already running. Most apps are a single open_app step; some need extra steps (dismiss splash, switch workspace).

default_dispatch_strategy.description: Ordered list of methods to try, cheapest first. The agent walks this until something resolves.

verification_default.description: Documents the verification family this app primarily uses. Informational only — not a runtime fallback, since shortcut.verification is required on every shortcut.

failure_recovery.description: Ordered list, least to most expensive. The chat LLM applies judgment within this menu when verification fails (see docs/architecture.md § Failure recovery flow). The `wait_for_idle` step (added Phase 7a, 2026-05-03) is appropriate for apps with loading states — re-attempt verify after the app finishes its current operation.

pre_step.description: Universal GUI-app-control primitive (Phase 7a, 2026-05-03). Optional. Action sequence executed before each shortcut's main `actions`. Used for known-modal dismissal (e.g. press escape, then click cancel-button if visible). Empty/absent for apps with clean session-start (VS Code). Used by Photoshop, AutoCAD, Figma, and other complex GUI apps where surprise modals (unsaved-changes prompts, format warnings, registration popups) are common. Read by the chat LLM when planning a shortcut execution; not enforced by the harness in v0.

keys.description: Either a single string (platform-resolved by the MCP) or a per-platform map.

text.description: May contain {parameter_name} placeholders that the MCP substitutes at execution time.

platform_specific.description: Workflow.open[] form: signals the MCP to use the app's detection block to launch.
